explain.say: Look around you. You may see a spoon, a glass of water and the air around you. Everything is made of matter. Matter comes in 3 main kinds: solid, liquid and gas. Look at the board. It sorts things into these 3 groups.

draw.text: Solid, liquid or gas? Sorting things around you

explain.say: Now look inside a solid. It is made of tiny bits called particles. They are far too small to see. In a solid, the particles are packed tight. They only wiggle in place. So a solid, like a rock or a spoon, keeps its shape.

Now look at the particles in a liquid. They are close together. But they can slide past each other. So a liquid flows. It takes the shape of its container, such as a cup or a bottle. Juice in a tall glass takes the shape of the glass.

Here are the particles in a gas. They are far apart. They move fast in every direction. So a gas spreads out to fill any space. The smell of fresh bread spreads through a whole house. Air is a gas. You cannot see air. Blow on your hand to feel it.

Look at the Liquids group again. Water is a liquid. Water can also be a solid or a gas. Freeze water and it becomes solid ice. Heat water and it becomes steam, a gas. Honey flows slowly, but honey is a liquid too.

faq.q: What is the difference between a solid, a liquid and a gas?
faq.a: A solid keeps its shape, because its particles are packed tight. A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container, because its particles slide past each other. A gas spreads out to fill any space, because its particles are far apart.
asks: What are the three states of matter?

faq.a: A solid is matter that keeps its own shape and size, like ice, wood, a rock or a spoon. Its particles are packed tightly and only wiggle in place.

faq.q: Why does a liquid take the shape of its container?
faq.a: The particles in a liquid stay close together but can slide over each other, so the liquid flows to fill the bottom of whatever it is in.
Yes. Air is a mixture of gases, mostly nitrogen and oxygen. We cannot see it, but we feel it as wind and need it to breathe.

faq.q: Can water be a solid, a liquid and a gas?
faq.a: Yes. Water is a solid when frozen into ice, a liquid in a glass, and a gas called water vapour or steam when heated.
asks: What are the three forms of water?

facts: Air is about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen.
Water is unusual: we meet it every day as a solid (ice), a liquid and a gas (water vapour).

quiz.say: Look at the 3 choices. Which one is a gas?
quiz.why: Steam is water as a gas. It spreads out into the air.

wrong.0: Milk is a liquid. It flows and takes the shape of the cup.
wrong.2: Ice is a solid. It keeps its shape.

quiz.say: A rock keeps its shape. Why?
quiz.show: 🪨 Why does a rock keep its shape?
quiz.why: A rock is a solid. Its particles are packed tight and only wiggle in place.

wrong.1: New ice keeps its shape too. Age does not matter.
wrong.2: A feather is light, and it keeps its shape too.
